description: INVERTED by issue #839 (maintainer ruling #833 rule 3, "nothing shadows"). The program is unchanged — `define forward … return 55 … end` then `print (fd 1 2)` — but its outcome is not. This fixture was authored by issue #787 as the OVER-APPLIED half of a host-crash regression: the reporter-position alias path had to reach the user procedure's ARITY guard and report `ol-too-many-inputs` with the CANONICAL `params.callable` `"forward"`, never the surface `"fd"`. It was marked TRANSITIONAL when it landed, because it needs a user procedure registered under a Heritage alias's canonical name, and every one of the thirteen canonicals is a built-in name. #839 adds the runtime phase-1 registration guard (`spec/execution-model.md:82-89`), so `define forward` now raises `ol-reserved-word` (`spec/error-model.md:125`) before phase 2 and the arity guard is never reached — the event stream is empty and no `ol-too-many-inputs` is produced at all. The fixture is kept and inverted rather than deleted: it is now the cheapest guard against the *precondition* silently coming back. Re-legalise `define forward` and this goes red, leading the next reader straight to #787. The evaluator invariant it used to prove — that the two chokepoints in one call path derive the same callee name — is carried forward at a lower level in `packages/runtime/src/heritage-alias-chokepoint.test.mjs`, which drives `evaluate()` over a hand-assembled `Environment` and so is unaffected by what registration admits. `params.callable`'s canonicalisation rule itself is unchanged and still pinned by `heritage-aliases-eval.test.mjs` against the BUILT-IN `forward`.

diagnostics.message: forward is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
